title: Heterogeneous climatic controls on tropical-forest biomass.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC: not open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links. Zenodo search on the title: 0 hits. Nature article page redirects to a login (paywalled; not scraped). HEAD on the ORNL DAAC (NASA's Oak Ridge data archive) GEDI L4A directory returned HTTP 401 (needs a NASA Earthdata login). NASA's collection metadata (CMR) confirms GEDI L4A Version 2.1 is a footprint-level 'aboveground biomass density' product (processing level 4, i.e. a modelled product).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract and press coverage (GEDI mission site, Smithsonian) only: about 16 million GEDI L4A biomass estimates for 2020 over intact lowland forest in the Amazon, Congo Basin and Southeast Asia, related to climate, soil, topography and storm covariates. I did not see a data availability statement, any deposited analysis table, or the covariate list.

a1_downloadable.note: The underlying GEDI L4A files need a NASA Earthdata login (HEAD returned HTTP 401). I found no deposited analysis table for the study (Zenodo 0 hits, no supplement in Europe PMC, article paywalled).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files. The footprint biomass value is a column in GEDI L4A, but the paper's analysis table (biomass plus matched climate, soil, topography and storm layers for each footprint) is not deposited as far as I found. It would have to be rebuilt by filtering to intact forest and spatially joining several gridded climate products.

a3_inputs_present.note: Climate, soil and topography covariates live in separate gridded products that would need extracting at each footprint location. Not verified.

a4_units_stated.note: From product documentation, not from opened files: GEDI L4A biomass density is in Mg/ha (megagrams per hectare).

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper says about 16 million footprints; count not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; GEDI L4A pantropical granules for one year are many GB of HDF5
a6_fits_laptop.note: Pulling a year of pantropical footprints plus covariate rasters is unlikely to fit a 5 GB working set without heavy subsetting. Estimate, not measured.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not check: no files opened.

a8_label_provenance.note: Killer. GEDI L4A biomass is not measured: it is a model's prediction, made by allometric regression models (fitted to field plots and airborne lidar) that convert the LiDAR (laser) canopy-height metrics into biomass. Learning it means copying that model, with its errors in tall and carbon-dense forests built in.

backbone.name: none; tabular geospatial covariates with no matching biology backbone
backbone.licence: GEDI data are NASA open data after free Earthdata registration

integration.partner_dataset: Field biomass plots (e.g. ForestPlots.net) would give a measured label, but access is permission-based
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do climate-biomass relationships learned from satellite-modelled biomass hold up against measured field-plot biomass?

honest_claim_h3: At best: predicts GEDI's own modelled biomass estimates from climate, soil and topography in intact lowland tropical forest in 2020, not measured biomass.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use climate, soil, topography and storm data at a forest location to predict how much above-ground plant biomass it holds.
plain_idea.train_on: Per laser footprint (a roughly 25 m spot): climate, soil, terrain and storm variables. The paper reports about 16 million footprints; not verified.
plain_idea.predict: Above-ground biomass in Mg/ha (megagrams per hectare). The 'truth' is itself a satellite model's estimate (GEDI L4A), converted from laser canopy-height measurements by allometric equations, not a field measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Carbon-cycle modellers want to know how forest carbon responds to warming and drought. But a model trained on another model's output adds little beyond the paper's own analysis.

ml_idea: Rejected. The considered task was regressing GEDI footprint biomass on climate, soil, topography and storm covariates, with a leave-one-continent-out transfer test. The label is a modelled product, the underlying data need a login, and the analysis table was not deposited.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A before any files were opened.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the authors deposited their footprint-by-covariate table openly. Even then, A8 (modelled label) stands.

verdict_reason: Fails A8 and A1. The biomass label is GEDI L4A, a modelled estimate from allometric equations applied to LiDAR (laser) canopy metrics, not a measurement. The raw files need a NASA Earthdata login (HTTP 401), and no analysis table was deposited (paywalled, 0 Zenodo hits). It is also a remote-sensing ecology topic, at the edge of the biology scope.
